Why a Tesla-SpaceX Merger Makes Strategic Sense On Wednesday, Tesla reported Q3 2026 earnings that were largely in line. EPS of $0.50 snuck by Wall Street expectations of $0.45. Meanwhile, revenue was flat year-over-year at $28.05 billion, matching Wall Street expectations. One bright spot was free cash flow. FCF of $1.53B - $3.99B signaled a rebound after sharply heavy CAPEX quarters, supporting $6.26B in operating cash flow. Auto margins rebounded to 18.1% from 16.3% on a more favorable product mix and higher Full Self-Driving (FSD) subscription revenues. Meanwhile, the energy segment remained a bright spot, with revenues surging 33%. The big takeaway is that CAPEX slowed to $4.73 billion (down from $5.79 billion in Q2) and Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles against 464,391 produced, keeping inventories low. Tesla has reached a maturity stage in its legacy EV business. Growth has steadied, but the company still generates strong cash flow. For the stock to break out, investors will want to see concrete progress on new growth avenues like Optimus, robotaxis, and Terafab. Shares are currently green in a blood-red tape, signaling robust relative strength. If Tesla shares can break above the 200-day moving average, it will signal a bullish trend change. Thoughts on Tesla/SpaceX Merger Elon Musk's comments during the SpaceX conference call confirmed that Tesla and SpaceX have formed independent special committees to explore a potential merger. For investors who have been following Musk's companies, the announcement is not a surprise. Months ago, Chamath Palihapitiya, a close friend and Musk investor, predicted a Tesla/SpaceX merger. Meanwhile, the Polymarket betting market suggests a 68% chance a Tesla/SpaceX merger will occur before the end of 2027. Why now? The stars have aligned perfectly for a merger for several reasons. First, a merger makes practical sense. With both Tesla and SpaceX becoming AI-first companies, their shared technical stack, consolidated compute, and integrated energy ecosystem are worth more as a synergy than a stand-alone entity. From a regulatory perspective, a merger also makes sense right now. Under President Biden, FTC Chair Lina Khan was known as an M&A hawk, striking down several big mergers. However, Musk's ties to the Trump administration could help his M&A aspirations. FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson has said that he plans to "get out of the way" of pro-competitive deals rather than mount opposition. Also, the combination makes sense from a financial perspective. Tesla has matured into a slower-growing but cash-rich company with a strong balance sheet. On the other hand, SpaceX is a hyper-growth company that faces enormous CAPEX concerns as it scales Starlink and Starship. Together, the two companies offer the magical elixir: Tesla's stable cash generation and SpaceX's massive revenue-growth trajectory.

Shares trade near $380 as I write, more than 21% below their record close of $489.88 in December 2025. On the surface, the quarter looked like progress. Operating income (what Tesla's business makes before interest and taxes) climbed to $718 million from $398 million in the second quarter. Management also cut its spending forecast for the year and said Megapack batteries are almost sold out for 2027. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » But I've learned to check where Tesla's profit came from before giving a quarter credit. And this time, a big share of it came from tariff refunds, which arguably say little about how the underlying business is doing. Image source: Getty Images. Showing how much Tesla's growth has slowed, third-quarter revenue was flat year over year at $28.0 billion -- a sharp deceleration. In the second quarter, revenue rose 26%, after a 16% gain in the first. Operating income fell 56% year over year, from around $1.6 billion, and the operating margin (the part of revenue left as operating profit) shrank to 2.6% from 5.8%. Net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) dropped 43% to $787 million. And non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share dipped 4% to $0.48. The more important detail is in Tesla's quarterly filing. After a Supreme Court ruling in February struck down certain tariffs, Tesla recognized $786 million in tariff refunds as lower costs in the third quarter. It also recorded $339 million it owes some energy storage customers as a reduction to revenue. Minus what Tesla owes these customers, the refunds added around $447 million to gross profit, or over 60% of the quarter's operating income. Take them out, and operating income would've been about $270 million -- under even the second quarter's $398 million. That matters because of the bar I set before this report. I said I'd want to see Tesla's operating income rebound show up in the results before buying shares. On a reported basis, it partly did. Without the refunds, I don't think it did. Sure, the call brought some good news, and the energy business was a big part of that. "We're actually almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027," CEO Elon Musk said in his opening comments.

Alphabet's strengths have made it the top dog in the digital advertising market for well over a decade, but a change could be on the horizon. Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Compounded at More Than 19% a Year Over 6 Decades, Nearly Double the S&P 500's 10% Return. Can Investors Still Apply That Playbook Today?

That amounts to compounded annual growth of about 19.9% -- nearly twice the gains of the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC), which delivered 10.4% an...

There will never be another Warren Buffett. From 1964 to 2024, the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB) achieved legendary returns of 5,502,284%. That amounts to compounded annual growth of about 19.9% -- nearly twice the gains of the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC), which delivered 10.4% annualized returns during those six decades. It's highly unlikely that anyone reading this can apply exactly the same playbook that Warren Buffett used to get rich. But there are a few key mindsets and model behaviors from Buffett's career that any investor can emulate. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Warren Buffett was not a penny-stock buyer. He didn't chase trends or follow fads. Instead, he bought stocks in companies that were often undervalued by the rest of the market. He owned stocks in high-quality companies with steady cash flows, strong business models he understood, and often sold products he personally used and/or enjoyed, like Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO). How to be like Buffett: Buy stocks in companies that you understand, that you believe in, that you're rooting for, and that you think can generate long-lasting returns. Buffett was not a short-term speculator or day trader. When he bought a company's stock, he typically intended to hold it for years. For great companies that Buffett really believed in, he said that his "favorite holding period is forever." Does this mean that you should never sell stocks? No. Sometimes investors need to take profits or cut losses. But this mindset shows how a long-term investing approach can help all kinds of investors build serious wealth -- even if they never reach Buffett's level of annualized returns. How to be like Buffett: Keep investing consistently and hold your stocks for the long term -- for 60 years or more, if you're lucky. Warren Buffett is perhaps the most successful stock picker of all time. His record of beating the market might never be beaten. But he also famously said that most people should buy low-cost S&P 500 index funds. Buying funds like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO) can serve as a strong foundation of an investment portfolio in a simple, low-fee way. You don't have to beat the market to get rich. If you want to choose individual stocks or sectors you're passionate about and enjoy following the markets and being a more active investor, that's totally fine. But many investors shouldn't try to be like Buffett. Instead, they should follow his advice and keep buying the S&P 500 regularly.

Most investors know Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB) is a combination of a portfolio of publicly traded stocks and privately owned businesses like GEICO Insurance, Duracell batteries, and Shaw flooring. Is it possible, however, that investors are underestimating just how much cash the conglomerate is collecting from one of its most boring wholly owned companies? It certainly looks that way. The business in question is the railroad BNSF, although you may know it better as Burlington Northern Santa Fe. Here's a closer look. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Contrary to a common assumption, Berkshire Hathaway isn't just a collection of companies that former CEO Warren Buffett and current CEO Greg Abel felt good about owning. Every one of its holdings serves a specific purpose. For instance, the vast majority of its privately held businesses are meant to generate reliable cash flow that backs up its insurance operation. Berkshire also discloses surprisingly detailed information about these businesses. For instance, through the first half of 2026, BNSF has generated just over $2.9 billion in operating earnings, up nearly 10% year over year. That's more than one-tenth of the organization's total operating earnings -- again. Although operating income is a key measure of a business's health, in this instance it's not necessarily the most meaningful one. Arguably more important to a conglomerate like Berkshire is how much cash an investment is reliably putting in its parent company's pockets, whether that investment is private or a publicly traded one. To this end, as Greg Abel noted in his 2025 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, published early this year, $4.4 billion of BNSF's $8.1 billion in 2025 operating earnings was handed over to Berkshire in the form of a cash dividend. The railroad company is on pace to at least match these numbers again this year, extending a long-standing track record of real cash generation. The amazing part? Berkshire Hathaway paid only $34.5 billion for BNSF back in 2010. Now 16 years later, the effective dividend yield on this initial investment is a healthy 12.7%, not to mention the appreciation of the railroad's value in the meantime. Although Berkshire itself doesn't offer a specific figure, estimates of its market value range from $75 billion to as much as $200 billion, and Buffett has been willing to say the railroad is the conglomerate's second-most-valuable asset, mostly due to the cash it produces.

JPMorgan interprets that development as potential preparation for a future shareholder vote involving a corporate combination. However, the proposed premium and ownership arrangements remain analytical scenarios rather than agreed transaction terms. JPMorgan believes a merger could bring together several business activities and technological capabilities already shared by Tesla and SpaceX. "The strategic logic for a combination remains coherent," Gupta wrote, citing the companies' shared engineering resources, artificial intelligence infrastructure, the Terafab semiconductor facility in Texas and Musk's involvement in both organisations. But analyst Doug Anmuth laid out another optimistic case, more than doubling his price target to $500 from $240, implying an upside of more than 200% from Wednesday's price. The reason? In a sentence: "No other company is as well positioned to go after the combined anticipated [total addressable market] of $28T+," Anmuth wrote in a note after earnings. In other words, SpaceX is going after everything. Musk's (current) favorite corporate child has already gone beyond rockets and satellites into telecommunications and a complete chip to data center to Grok vertical integration AI, which has overtaken the rest of SpaceX's operations to become its biggest business by revenue. Alone, these businesses would be huge. Together, they approach a quarter of US GDP. Just imagine if robotaxi and robotics markets get tacked on to that. In the corporate world, focus often means success — finding the right product, targeting the right customers, and defining the specific value your firm brings. But when you're a giant tech conglomerate, your lane extends to market conquest. Everything is up for grabs, and the name of the game is planting flags. The space race, the AI race, and even, for Musk, the telecom race and supplanting legacy carriers like AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS). All of this makes the Tesla (TSLA) angle especially interesting. If SpaceX is already on its way to the moon, why not merge with an EV, robotics, and robotaxi company too? The boards of both companies have formed special committees to explore a tie-up. Yet another reason why Musk's enormous ambitions and SpaceX's promising start as a publicly traded company can prompt such lofty projections. On the company's earnings call Tuesday, Musk said he projects SpaceX's annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 to fall "somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion." This quarter gave us a hint of where things are going, revealing how, in the span of a few months, SpaceX morphed into a new, AI-forward company. Plans to increase local business banker coverage by 11% and expand Coaching for Impact program to graduate more than 700 Atlanta-area entrepreneurs over the next five years. Provide a $10 million long-term, low-cost financing to Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs (ACE) aimed at financing approximately 70 small business loans across Georgia, with at least $7.5 million deployed in Metro Atlanta. ATLANTA, October 21, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--At Chase for Business' Make Your Move Summit in Atlanta, JPMorganChase today announced significantly expanded efforts to support Atlanta small businesses, including hiring more local business bankers, growing its Coaching for Impact program and making a $10 million long-term, low-cost loan to ACE | Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs, Inc. (ACE) to help qualifying, local small businesses obtain flexible financing. This work is a part of the firm's American Dream Initiative, a multi-year effort aimed at scaling evidence-based, local solutions to help expand opportunities for communities, including a firmwide effort to power 10 million small businesses nationwide—up from seven million served today—over the next several years with expanded banker presence, access to the capital, coaching, tools, and practical policy support they need to thrive. "Small business owners are getting healthier and more disciplined, but their growth and success are dependent on having a strong support team, including the right banker," said Stevie Baron, CEO of Chase for Business. "We want to match the grit and determination of Atlanta's entrepreneurs with proven, local resources that help them address barriers head-on, as well as connect them to capital, coaching and tools that help them grow and hire." Powering small business growth through local hiring and coaching As a part of the American Dream Initiative, JPMorganChase is growing its support for small businesses nationwide including increasing its business banker coverage in Atlanta by 11% over the next five years. Business bankers work directly with business owners, providing access to capital and valuable resources and connections that help small businesses start and scale with confidence. Chase for Business plans to grow its team of Senior Business Consultants nationwide, including in Atlanta, to help expand the firm's Coaching for Impact program. Coaching for Impact provides small businesses with expanded access to complimentary one-on-one consulting, executive coaching and on-demand education tailored to their specific needs. More than 15,000 business owners and entrepreneurs around the U.S. have graduated from the program since its launch—including more than 450 from Atlanta. Over the next five years, the firm plans to graduate more than 700 Atlanta-based business owners and entrepreneurs through the program.

JPMorgan issues its first long-term Bitcoin return forecast

No summary available

JPMorgan Chase's money managers think the best investment of the next decade could be the one their boss once called a "pet rock." JPMorgan Asset Management, the investment arm of America's largest bank, said this week that it expects Bitcoin to generate an annual return of about 10% over the next ...

JPMorgan Chase's money managers think the best investment of the next decade could be the one their boss once called a "pet rock." JPMorgan Asset Management, the investment arm of America's largest bank, said this week that it expects Bitcoin to generate an annual return of about 10% over the next 10-15 years. That's more than it expects from U.S. stocks, at 7.5%, and nearly twice what it sees for gold, at 5.5%. The forecast sits in the firm's 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, a yearly report that big pension funds and endowments use to plan their portfolios. It has been published for 31 years. This is the first time Bitcoin has been in it. JPMorgan isn't telling anyone to buy it, though. The same report says Bitcoin swings about three times as much as the stock market and keeps it out of the firm's model portfolios. Related: JPMorgan's answer to the stablecoin threat is here JPMorgan Asset Management expects Bitcoin to return about 10% a year over the next 10 to 15 years, according to the report's assumptions table. No other major investment on that table comes close. The firm expects U.S. real estate investment trusts to return 8.2% a year and U.S. small-company stocks 7.7%. Large U.S. stocks, the kind that make up the S&P 500, come in at 7.5%. U.S. bonds are at 5.6% and gold at 5.5%. The stock forecast itself went up this year. The firm raised its large-cap estimate to 7.5% from 6.7%. Gold's estimate didn't move. JPMorgan Asset Management The catch is in the next column over. JPMorgan puts Bitcoin's volatility, a measure of how much its price swings, at 55%. Large U.S. stocks sit at 18% and gold at 17.2%. By the firm's own numbers, Bitcoin moves about three times as much as the stock market. That's also why the report lists two return figures for Bitcoin. Its simple average return is 20.9%. The 10% figure accounts for the damage that deep drops incur over time, and it's the number JPMorgan uses for comparison. The firm says Bitcoin is "not included as an allocation," meaning it isn't recommending any portion of a portfolio go into it. Bitcoin also isn't part of the report's main portfolio models. JPMorgan analyzed it separately with a smaller group of public market assets. It said Bitcoin's price swings, and the way it moves unpredictably against stocks and bonds, make it hard to build into a long-term plan. The report also pushed back on a common argument from crypto supporters: that a weakening U.S. dollar will push investors into digital assets in large numbers.

No summary available

Bitcoin just earned a spot in one of Wall Street's most closely watched return forecasts, and it landed at the top of the table. J.P. Morgan Asset Management projected a 10% compound annual return for Bitcoin over the next 10 to 15 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, released Mo...

Bitcoin just earned a spot in one of Wall Street's most closely watched return forecasts, and it landed at the top of the table. J.P. Morgan Asset Management projected a 10% compound annual return for Bitcoin over the next 10 to 15 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, released Monday. It's the 31st annual edition of the report and the first to include Bitcoin. The forecast tops the firm's projections for U.S. large-cap stocks at 7.5%, gold at 5.5% and a classic 60/40 stock-bond portfolio at 7%. The catch is volatility. The report pegs Bitcoin's annualized volatility at 55%, compared with about 17% for gold. That's why Bitcoin's arithmetic average return, a simple average of yearly gains, comes in at 20.9%, more than double the compound figure investors would actually keep after big price swings. The firm stopped short of adding Bitcoin to the models it uses to map how assets move together. "For the first time, we put a range on bitcoin returns, though we do not yet include bitcoin in our main covariance matrices," the report says. Instead, JPMorgan built a separate, smaller matrix comparing Bitcoin with a subset of assets, citing the cryptocurrency's volatility and unstable correlations as obstacles to widespread portfolio inclusion. JPMorgan also pushed back on a popular bull case, calling the idea that currency debasement will spark a rush into crypto "wide of the mark." Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan welcomed the forecast, if not every input. "First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight at you, then they add you to their Long-Term Capital Markets Assumptions paper and predict you'll be the best-performing asset of the next decade," he wrote on X. Hougan argued that JPMorgan's 55% volatility assumption is too high, which in turn makes its return forecast too conservative. Bitwise, which manages crypto index funds and ETFs, has a stake in that view. The forecast comes as JPMorgan deepens its own blockchain bets. The bank is bringing JPM Coin, a token representing dollar deposits, to Ethereum, and has joined BlackRock, Goldman Sachs and the DTCC in tokenized stock efforts. JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain The timing is notable. Bitcoin could outperform both US stocks and gold over the next decade, according to a striking new projection from JPMorgan Asset Management. The Wall Street giant estimates that Bitcoin (BTC) could deliver annual returns of 10% in its base-case scenario, comfortably ahead of the 7.5% expected from US large-cap stocks and 5.5% from gold. At that rate, a $10,000 Bitcoin investment would grow to nearly $26,000 over ten years, assuming the projected returns compound annually. Yet JPMorgan considers a decade-long Bitcoin forecast premature and continues to exclude BTC from its core risk models. The figures appear in the 2027 edition of JPMorgan Asset Management's Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (LTCMA). The annual report has never before put a range on Bitcoin returns. The base case starts from a spot price of $83,000 as of September 30. The bull case reaches 16.6% a year. Its range also includes a bear case of -11.2% a year. BeInCrypto calculations show what those rates imply for Bitcoin's price by 2036, compounded from $83,000. The base case of 10% a year points to about $215,000. The bull case of 16.6% a year points to about $386,000. The bear case of -11.2% a year points to about $25,000. "BTC mostly trades like a high beta risk asset that tracks global money supply growth, but it is sometimes treated as digital gold. Unstable correlations with other assets present a modeling hurdle. A further challenge is forecasting an asset whose fundamentals are not cash flows and whose economics may be as much about adoption, regulation and liquidity as technology," the analysts wrote. JPMorgan cites those correlations and very high volatility for keeping BTC in a separate illustrative table. SINGAPORE, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Visa, a global leader in digital payments and the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) have signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to strengthen Singapore's appeal as a preferred travel destination and to unlock new growth opportunities. The collaboration will focus on three key pillars – driving discovery of Singapore's tourism products, especially its dining and night-time experiences; deriving insights to identify high-value tourism opportunities; and developing co-branded marketing campaigns to build brand preference for both Visa and Singapore. Visa also announced that Singapore will be part of Visa Destinations, and the collaboration will leverage Visa Destinations as a platform to introduce strategic partnerships, flagship initiatives and experiences across Singapore's tourism precincts and high-yield traveller segments. Visa Destinations is a global travel programme designed to elevate how travellers discover and experience the world's most iconic destinations. Singapore is the second country to launch Visa Destinations in Asia Pacific, following Thailand which was introduced in July this year. Other cities include London, New York, and Paris, reinforcing the city's position as a leading travel hub. The programme will commence in Singapore in November this year. Curating distinctively local experiences to inspire discovery of Singapore The first pillar of collaboration will focus on benefits and experiences for travellers across tourism industries including attractions, dining, entertainment, retail and tours, which are key categories of spend. Visa's data shows that shopping and dining are significant contributors to traveller spend. This reinforces the importance of curating meaningful experiences that give travellers compelling reasons to return to Singapore, particularly as repeat visitors spend approximately four times more than first-time visitors[1]. Visa's spend trend data and insights can sharpen the understanding of visitor segments, source markets and experiences with the greatest potential to drive higher-value demand, deeper exploration and repeat travel. Visa and STB will also work closely to curate offers that showcase local businesses across tourism precincts, including building on an existing partnership with Pelago by Singapore Airlines to promote attractions and tours, supported by seamless, secure payment experiences throughout the visitor journey. These include introducing benefits and experience packages for Visa cardholders globally through the Visa Destinations platform at key attractions in Singapore.

What's at stake: The credit card companies announce third-quarter earnings next week, and investors will be looking at revenue sources such as value-added non-payment services. With card-issuing banks pressured to build strategies for agentic commerce and digital assets, Visa and Mastercard are expanding their abilities to sell into these trends. Both card brands have released services in the past few days, and in the case of Visa, there were rumors of a potential $2.5 billion deal to acquire cryptocurrency technology firm Fireblocks. Visa said it does not comment on rumors or speculation. "We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true," a Fireblocks spokesperson said in an email. Even before talk of a Fireblocks acquisition, Visa recently released several tools designed for agentic commerce and digital assets. Earlier this week, the card company introduced services for corporate payments, including new analytics for supplier spending, virtual-card fraud prevention, and a live pilot enabling trusted AI agents to complete B2B invoice payments. "The B2B world is filled with very routine manual processes that are just begging for automation," Darren Parslow, global head of Visa Commercial Solutions, told American Banker. The new analytics, called SESA 2.0, use AI to produce spend analysis and to help businesses identify high-potential supplier opportunities. Another product, Visa Commercial Fraud Solutions, helps issuers and businesses validate suppliers, authenticate virtual-card payment activity and apply controls before a payment is approved. "What we're really trying to do is build the ecosystem for agentic commerce," Parslow said. An additional initiative, a pilot with Billtrust, enables trusted AI agents to initiate and help complete approved invoice payments through supplier portals, using Visa Intelligent Commerce and Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol. "What's great about this pilot is it addresses both sides, the buyers and suppliers, for a fully automated payment from invoice approval to supplier acceptance," Parslow said. On the digital asset front, Visa this week took its Visa Direct stablecoin project out of pilot testing. In the initial deployment, Inyo Global, a Visa Direct processor that has banks, fintechs and payment companies among its clients, is supporting stablecoin processing for Visa Direct clients and partners. These businesses will have the option to prefund cross-border payouts through Visa Direct with USDC in near real time, rather than relying solely on traditional funding windows.

Visa Inc (NYSE:V, XETRA:3V64) and Mastercard Inc (NYSE:MA) could generate a growing stream of revenue from payment tokenization as digital transactions expand and card networks charge for technology that helps secure payments and reduce fraud, according to UBS. Analysts estimated that tokenization-related revenue could contribute a low-single-digit percentage to total net revenue growth at both companies over the medium term, with a low-to-mid-single-digit percentage contribution to growth in their value-added services businesses. The analysts estimated Visa's contribution is currently moderately higher than Mastercard's, partly reflecting pricing changes Visa has recently introduced or announced. Tokenization replaces sensitive card details with unique digital identifiers, allowing payments to be processed without exposing the underlying card number. The technology is used across eCommerce, mobile wallets and stored payment credentials, with potential applications in emerging areas such as agentic commerce, where artificial intelligence systems initiate transactions on behalf of consumers. UBS said the card networks are increasingly monetizing tokenization through dedicated fees, pricing structures that favor tokenized transactions and broader digital services that incorporate token-related capabilities. The resulting revenue growth reflects a combination of rising card-not-present transaction volumes, greater token adoption within those transactions and pricing for the services provided. Many tokenization-related fees are reported within Visa's value-added services business and Mastercard's value-added services and solutions segment, although some revenue may be recognized within their core payments network businesses. Pricing opportunities ahead UBS sees scope for Visa and Mastercard to increase tokenization-related pricing as their product offerings develop and become more valuable in preventing fraud and enabling new forms of digital commerce. The bank's analysis includes fees already implemented or announced by the companies, as well as publicly disclosed future pricing changes. It therefore views its estimates as a conservative starting point, with additional fees or pricing increases representing potential upside. Visa has introduced or announced several tokenization-related fees that Mastercard has not, including fees for tokenized card-present transactions in the US and plans to expand its Digital Commerce Service Fee into Europe in 2027. Visa has also announced a 2027 increase to its Digital Commerce Service Fee, according to UBS.

Fireblocks Denies $2.5 Billion Visa Buyout Claims

No summary available

Earlier today, Axios reported that Visa is in late-stage talks to acquire crypto infrastructure company Fireblocks for around $2.5 billion. Fireblocks has rejected the claim. "We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true at present ...

Earlier today, Axios reported that Visa is in late-stage talks to acquire crypto infrastructure company Fireblocks for around $2.5 billion. Fireblocks has rejected the claim. "We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true at present time," a Fireblocks spokesperson told BeInCrypto. The reported price also raises questions. Fireblocks raised $550 million at an $8 billion valuation in January 2022. A $2.5 billion sale would be almost 70% below that figure, although private fundraising valuations and acquisition prices are not directly comparable. Fireblocks makes software that lets banks, crypto exchanges, and payment companies securely hold and move digital assets. Its technology protects crypto wallets, controls who can approve transfers and connects businesses to blockchain networks. For example, a payment provider can use Fireblocks to send stablecoins overseas without building its own blockchain security infrastructure. Fireblocks says more than $300 billion in stablecoins moved across its systems each month on average over the past year. That is transaction volume, not company revenue. Visa already has an established global payments network. Owning Fireblocks could give it ready-made technology and relationships with businesses developing stablecoin payment services. The timing would be significant. Visa launched its own stablecoin platform in July and moved a stablecoin-powered Visa Direct funding service into commercial production this month. Rival Mastercard completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK in August. If the rumored deal ever materialized, it could accelerate the shift toward blockchain-based payments and increase competition between card networks for institutional stablecoin business. It would also raise a sensitive question for Fireblocks' customers, some of whom compete with Visa: Would a Visa-owned Fireblocks remain a neutral technology provider? For now, Fireblocks says the reported talks are not happening. Read the Original story Fireblocks Denies $2.5 Billion Visa Buyout Claims by Mohammad Shahid at beincrypto.com

Wall Street Analysts Think Visa (V) Is a Good Investment: Is It?

No summary available

When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important? Let's take a look at what these Wall Stre...

When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important? Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Visa (V) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage. Visa currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.24, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 41 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.24 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy. Of the 41 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 34 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 82.9% and 9.8% of all recommendations. Check price target & stock forecast for Visa here>>> While the ABR calls for buying Visa, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential. Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations. In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement. With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision. Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether. Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The proven Zacks Rank puts an emphasis on earnings estimates and estimate revisions, while our Style Scores work to identify stocks with specific traits. Right now, both Wex and Visa are sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy). This means that both companies have witnessed positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that both of these stocks have an improving earnings outlook. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors. Value investors also try to analyze a wide range of traditional figures and metrics to help determine whether a company is undervalued at its current share price levels. Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use. WEX currently has a forward P/E ratio of 9.35, while V has a forward P/E of 27.21. We also note that WEX has a PEG ratio of 0.83. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. V currently has a PEG ratio of 1.92. Another notable valuation metric for WEX is its P/B ratio of 4.75. The P/B ratio is used to compare a stock's market value with its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. For comparison, V has a P/B of 21. These metrics, and several others, help WEX earn a Value grade of A, while V has been given a Value grade of D. Both WEX and V are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that WEX is the superior value option right now. RESTON, Va., Sept. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today issued a letter to shareholders from Lightbridge's Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Seth Grae, following the Company's selection for the U.S. Department of Energy's Launch Pad INL Program. Dear Shareholders, Recently, we announced that Lightbridge has been selected to participate in the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) Launch Pad program at Idaho National Laboratory (INL). This is an important milestone for our Company that can enable an accelerated pathway for the commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel™. In this letter, I want to provide additional context on the significance of this milestone and convey why we believe we will look back on this day as one of the most consequential milestones in Lightbridge's history. What makes this milestone so significant for Lightbridge? DOE's Launch Pad INL enables a new two-prong commercialization strategy. The Special HALEU Extrusion Demonstration (SHED) facility that will produce Lead Test Assemblies (LTAs) will be deployed under DOE authorization. The Lightbridge Expandable Fuel Facility (LEFF) will proceed separately toward U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) licensing for commercial-scale production (see below). This two-pronged approach can accelerate our time-to-market by several years compared to our previous projections. While detailed cost estimates for SHED are still being developed, based on preliminary estimates, we currently expect our existing cash and financial resources to be sufficient to fund the construction, operation, and decommissioning of SHED. The path for SHED goes through the DOE. The path for LEFF runs through the NRC. Which one applies depends on the facility's scale and purpose. SHED, a pilot-scale facility that produces LTAs, the full-size assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel that a utility would load into the core of an operating commercial reactor, which the NRC treats as part of a testing program, does not require an NRC license. LEFF, a commercial-scale fuel fabrication facility, does. We've previously described LEFF as the world's first fuel fabrication plant designed to expand in capacity as commercial demand for our fuel grows. Our original plan was to build LEFF under an NRC license in stages, starting with pilot-scale fabrication to produce LTAs, and then expand production to commercial scale to support batch reloads. That path is well understood from a regulatory licensing standpoint but would cost substantially more and take much longer.

RESTON, Va., Sept. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR) was deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ambassador (ret.) Thomas Graham Jr., at the age of 92. He served as Executive Chairman of the Company's Board of Directors from 2009 to 2022 and as Chairman from 2022 to 2024. A defining figure in Lightbridge's history, Ambassador Graham devoted nearly two decades to the Company and brought a career centered on American arms control and nuclear non-proliferation policy. A graduate of Princeton University and Harvard Law School, Ambassador Graham served as a senior U.S. diplomat involved in every major international arms control and non-proliferation negotiation in which the United States participated between 1970 and 1997 — including the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks, the START I and START II Treaties, the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, the Conventional Armed Forces in Europe Treaty, and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty. He spent 15 years as general counsel of the U.S. Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and served as its Acting Director in 1993. Appointed by President Clinton as Special Representative of the President for Arms Control, Non-Proliferation, and Disarmament from 1994 to 1997, he led the U.S. government's effort that secured the permanent extension of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in 1995. Ambassador Graham joined Lightbridge as Executive Chairman in 2009 and helped shape the Company's founding proposition: that advanced nuclear fuel technology could improve the economics and safety of nuclear power while strengthening proliferation resistance. He carried creative thinking relating to non-proliferation well beyond the boardroom — as an appointee to the United Arab Emirates' International Advisory Board on nuclear energy from 2009 to 2016, as co-author of Seeing the Light: The Case for Nuclear Power in the 21st Century, and as Co-Chairman of the Atlantic Council's Nuclear Energy and National Security Coalition. Across fifteen books and more than 100 published articles, he made the case that non-proliferation and the expansion of civil nuclear energy were not competing goals. He was named Chairman Emeritus of Lightbridge in 2024 and retired from the Company the following year. Seth Grae, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge Corporation: "Tom's name on our board did something no business plan could: it told governments, regulators, and investors that a company working on nuclear fuel took non-proliferation seriously as a first principle. He negotiated the treaties that shaped the nuclear order and spent his last two decades arguing that the same seriousness could make nuclear energy larger, not smaller. He asked hard questions at every board meeting I attended with him, and Lightbridge is a better, more credible company for it. On behalf of our Board of Directors and our entire team, I extend our deepest condolences to his family." RESTON, Va., Sept. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the Japan Patent Office ("JPO") for Japanese Patent Application No. 20...

RESTON, Va., Sept. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the Japan Patent Office ("JPO") for Japanese Patent Application No. 2024-513980, titled "Multi-Zone Fuel Element." The allowed claims cover the fuel element design itself, a fuel assembly incorporating that design, and a method of producing the element through additive manufacturing (3D printing), extending protection for a core element of Lightbridge Fuel into a market with one of the world's largest nuclear power markets. The patent covers a fuel rod composed of three layers of different materials, with each layer varying in thickness along the rod's length. That shape can be designed to control how the fuel behaves at different points inside the reactor, improving performance and safety margins. The claims also cover the fuel assembly into which these rods go and the 3D printing method used to build them. Japan has 32 reactors classified as operable, of which 15 have received clearance from the country's Nuclear Regulation Authority and returned to service, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Japan's national energy plan targets nuclear power at approximately 20% of electricity generation by fiscal year 2040, which would require up to 30 reactors in operation. "Japan operates a significant nuclear fleet and has made nuclear power central to its energy security and decarbonization policy, which makes it an important market for us," said Seth Grae, Chairman & CEO of Lightbridge Corporation. "This decision covers the fuel rod and the assembly that holds it, and the additive manufacturing method that produces it. That three-way coverage matters commercially because it protects the fuel product, which a utility will actually load into a reactor, and the process we intend to use to produce it." Lightbridge's fuel technology is backed by an extensive worldwide patent portfolio spanning jurisdictions representing the majority of global nuclear generating capacity. About Lightbridge Corporation Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR) is focused on developing advanced nuclear fuel technology essential to delivering abundant, zero-emission, clean energy and providing energy security to the world. The Company is developing Lightbridge Fuel™, a proprietary next-generation nuclear fuel technology for existing light-water and pressurized heavy-water reactors, significantly enhancing reactor safety, economics, and proliferation resistance. The Company is also developing Lightbridge Fuel for new small modular reactors to deliver the same benefits, when combined with load-following with renewables, on a zero-carbon electric grid.

Provides an Accelerated Pathway toward DOE Authorization to Manufacture Lead Test Assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel for Operation in Commercial Power Reactors RESTON, Va., Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fue...

Provides an Accelerated Pathway toward DOE Authorization to Manufacture Lead Test Assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel for Operation in Commercial Power Reactors RESTON, Va., Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has been selected to participate in the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad INL, administered by the U.S. Department of Energy's ("DOE") National Reactor Innovation Center ("NRIC") at Idaho National Laboratory ("INL"). Selection provides an accelerated pathway toward DOE authorization for Lightbridge to design, build, and operate a dedicated facility at INL to manufacture Lead Test Assemblies ("LTAs") of Lightbridge Fuel — the Company's proprietary metallic nuclear fuel — for testing in U.S. commercial power reactors. LTAs represent the final fuel qualification stage between reactor testing and commercial fuel sales. Lightbridge now has an accelerated pathway to establishing manufacturing capability for producing LTAs. The selection marks the most significant advance to date in Lightbridge's path from fuel testing to commercial deployment. By establishing a dedicated manufacturing facility under DOE authorization, the Company expects to significantly shorten the timeline for producing LTAs for operation in a commercial U.S. reactor. "This is the most important step we have taken toward putting Lightbridge Fuel into commercial reactors, and it changes how investors should understand our timeline," said Seth Grae, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge. "A DOE-authorized facility will let us manufacture full-scale Lightbridge Fuel assemblies that nuclear utilities will run in their plants, and can produce them years sooner than a conventional facility licensing path would allow. We have been working with a major engineering, procurement, and construction ("EPC") firm in preparation for the start of construction of the Special High-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) Extrusion Demonstration (SHED) facility as soon as next year. Our goal is for Lightbridge Fuel to become the standard fuel that produces most of the world's nuclear energy, and this is where that path begins." Launch Pad is a DOE initiative supporting the Trump administration's goal of widescale nuclear energy expansion through streamlined pathways for developers to demonstrate and accelerate commercial deployment. Facilities developed under the program are privately financed. Lightbridge continues to develop detailed cost estimates for SHED, and based on preliminary estimates, the anticipated cost to construct, operate, and decommission SHED can be funded from the Company's current cash and financial resources.

Seth Grae, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge, commented, "In the first half of 2026, our fuel development work at Idaho National Laboratory produced its first irradiated material for examination. In May, the first batch of our fuel material samples was removed from the Advanced Test Reactor with members of our engineering team and senior management present. Those samples are now cooling ahead of post-irradiation examination (PIE), which we expect to begin later this year. The PIE will produce our first material property data under high burn-up conditions, while irradiation of the remaining samples continues. "In May, we partnered with Studsvik Scandpower to develop an extension of the Studsvik CMS5 Core Management Suite to model the new Lightbridge Fuel™ design, placing our design inside the state-of-the-art software that utilities already rely on worldwide. Then in June, I represented Lightbridge at the White House launch of UPRISE, the Department of Energy initiative targeting approximately 5 GW of end capacity drawn from reactors already operating. As electricity demand accelerates, driven by AI and hyperscale data centers, the fastest and least expensive additional nuclear-generated megawatts will come from increasing the power output of currently operating reactors. Lightbridge Fuel is being designed to deliver the largest power uprates available while enhancing safety and operating at approximately 1,000°C cooler than conventional fuel." "Since the quarter end, we signed a memorandum of understanding with Quadrant Nuclear Industries to establish a framework for long-term HALEU supply from its planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory. Securing domestic fuel supply is work that has to be done years before the fuel is needed, and we intend to be early rather than late. Companies to explore long-term HALEU supply arrangements supporting the commercialization of next-generation nuclear fuel technologies RESTON, Va. and BOSTON, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR), a leader in advanced nuclear fuel technology, and Quadrant Nuclear Industries Inc. (QNI), a developer of integrated nuclear fuel cycle capabilities, today announced they have entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish a framework for collaboration on the long-term supply of high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel. The MoU reflects a shared commitment to strengthening the domestic nuclear fuel supply chain, advancing next-generation nuclear technologies, and supporting U.S. energy security and decarbonization objectives. Under the agreement, Lightbridge and QNI will engage in discussions regarding the potential supply and long-term offtake of HALEU produced at QNI's planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory. "We are pleased to establish this Memorandum of Understanding with QNI as we continue advancing the commercialization of Lightbridge Fuel™," said Seth Grae, Chairman and CEO of Lightbridge Corporation. "As we progress in the development and regulatory licensing of Lightbridge Fuel™, it is critical that we begin solidifying a reliable domestic supply of HALEU. We look forward to working with QNI to explore opportunities that support our long-term fuel requirements and contribute to a more secure U.S. nuclear fuel supply chain." "Developing a secure, U.S.-based source of HALEU is essential to enabling the next generation of nuclear energy," said Dee Mewbourne, CEO of QNI. "Our cooperation with Lightbridge reflects the growing alignment between advanced fuel innovation and domestic fuel production. Through this collaboration, we aim to establish a framework for a long-term offtake arrangement that supports commercialization of Lightbridge's advanced fuel technology while strengthening the domestic nuclear fuel ecosystem." QNI is developing an integrated HALEU production capability in coordination with the U.S. Department of Energy and other key stakeholders. Its planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory is designed to produce up to eighteen metric tons of HALEU annually at full capacity, supporting both commercial and government markets for advanced nuclear reactors. The companies intend to collaborate on areas including fuel supply planning, technical interface requirements, commercial structuring, regulatory coordination, and logistics considerations associated with HALEU supply arrangements.

The samples were removed on May 6, 2026, with Lightbridge's full-time fuel engineering team and senior management — 24 Lightbridge personnel in total — on site at INL for the milestone. On May 7, the Lightbridge team met with the INL personnel leading the project, including John Wagner, Laboratory Director of Idaho National Laboratory, and Jess Gehin, Associate Lab Director. Lightbridge discussed progress to date and the path forward across multiple Lightbridge projects currently underway at INL. "The data already developed at the Advanced Test Reactor is a meaningful validation of the innovation and engineering behind Lightbridge Fuel," said Seth Grae, President and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge. "The data to be collected during the planned post-irradiation examination are expected to support our ongoing fuel performance modeling activities and regulatory licensing efforts for commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel. We are grateful to Lab Director John Wagner, Associate Lab Director Jess Gehin, and the entire INL team for the operational excellence that has made this campaign possible." The FAST method was conceived and developed at INL. Geoffrey "Boone" Beausoleil, Lightbridge's Director of Materials, played a key role on the INL team that originated the initial concept for FAST and developed the underlying testing methodology during his prior tenure at INL. Image 2: Several members of Lightbridge team looking over the ATR canal (May 6, 2026) The samples that have been removed from the ATR will undergo post-irradiation examination to collect the data on fundamental material properties under high-burnup irradiation conditions. The data developed will support the broader testing program aimed at confirming the safety, performance, and economic advantages of Lightbridge Fuel relative to conventional nuclear fuel used in commercial reactors worldwide.

Together, Lightbridge and Studsvik will provide the commercial nuclear sector with a software package for light water reactors (LWRs) that is fully supported by the state-of-the-art Studsvik software already adopted by customers around the world. Lightbridge is developing a next-generation nuclear fuel design, Lightbridge Fuel, to improve the economics, safety, and proliferation resistance of existing and new reactors. The design includes metallic fuel rods that will be more economical and safer than traditional fuel. "As we advance our efforts to license Lightbridge Fuel for use in commercial nuclear power plants, we are pleased to leverage Studsvik's CMS5 software to help drive these initiatives forward," said Seth Grae, President and CEO of Lightbridge. "We are pleased to partner with Lightbridge as they take this important step in advancing the licensing of their next-generation fuel product," said Art Wharton, President of the Studsvik Scandpower Group. "Studsvik Scandpower remains committed to continuously enhancing our software capabilities to support the nuclear industry's growth and the development of innovative fuel technologies." This partnership further strengthens Lightbridge and Studsvik's position in the global nuclear industry. About Studsvik Studsvik provides a range of advanced technical services to the global nuclear power industry. Our core areas of expertise include fuel and materials technology, software for core monitoring and fuel optimisation, decommissioning and radiation protection services, as well as technical solutions for the handling, conditioning, and volume reduction of radioactive waste. The company has over 75 years of experience in nuclear technology and services in radiological environments. Studsvik employs approximately 540 people across 7 countries and is listed on the Nasdaq Stockholm. About Lightbridge Corporation Lightbridge Corporation (NASDAQ: LTBR) is focused on developing advanced nuclear fuel technology essential to delivering abundant, zero-emission, clean energy and providing energy security to the world. The Company is developing Lightbridge Fuel™, a proprietary next-generation nuclear fuel technology for existing light-water and pressurized heavy-water reactors, significantly enhancing reactor safety, economics, and proliferation resistance. The Company is also developing Lightbridge Fuel for new small modular reactors to deliver the same benefits, plus load-following with renewables, on a zero-carbon electric grid.

RESTON, Va., April 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, announced its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, and provided an update on the Company's continued progress. Seth Grae, President & Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge, commented, "The first quarter of 2026 reflects the depth and pace of Lightbridge's program execution. We received patent allowances from three major jurisdictions—Canada, the United States, and the European Patent Office—expanding the scope of patent protection for Lightbridge Fuel™ across the CANDU fleet, the U.S. domestic light water reactor market, and 39 European contracting states. We also entered into an engineering contract with Stern Laboratories to launch a multi-phase thermal-hydraulics test program to support U.S. regulatory licensing of our fuel for light water reactors. We were selected to serve on the Industry Advisory Board of a $6 million DOE-funded research initiative at Penn State. And our technical team presented proprietary uranium-zirconium alloy research at TMS2026, contributing to the scientific foundation that underpins everything we are building." "We believe this is the most promising time for the growth of nuclear power in decades. Record global generation in 2025, sweeping U.S. executive action to accelerate reactor permitting and NRC reform, and landmark procurement commitments from the world's largest technology companies have collectively shifted the industry from a question of 'if' to a question of 'when and how fast.' Lightbridge is building to be the answer to the 'how'—specifically, how the existing global reactor fleet and new-build water-cooled reactors deliver more power and further enhanced safety, with improved economics." "Our program is advancing on every front. We have grown to over two dozen in-house engineers across all of our core disciplines, including neutronics, thermal hydraulics, fuel performance, materials, fuel assembly mechanical design, licensing, high-performance computing, and program management, and we continue to add talent. The qualification pathway ahead of us is well-defined. We expect Lightbridge Fuel will enable power uprates of up to 30% or more for new-build water-cooled reactors, meaningfully more than any other approach, while operating approximately 1,000 degrees Celsius cooler. In existing light-water reactors, Lightbridge Fuel is expected to enable power uprates of up to 20% or more (depending on balance-of-plant constraints) and to extend the fuel cycle length. In addition to creating new nuclear generating capacity, the world is seeking greater power from the infrastructure it already has. That is precisely the problem we've designed Lightbridge Fuel to solve."

Lightbridge Receives Notice of Allowance for European Patent Covering Multi-Zone Fuel Element and Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) Method

No summary available

RESTON, Va., April 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that the European Patent Office (EPO) has issued a Notice of Allowance for European Patent Application No. 22777419.7,...

RESTON, Va., April 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that the European Patent Office (EPO) has issued a Notice of Allowance for European Patent Application No. 22777419.7, titled "Multi-Zone Fuel Element." The allowed patent covers Lightbridge's proprietary nuclear fuel element design, featuring multiple radial zones with variable thicknesses along the axial direction, enabling precise control of neutron flux distribution throughout the fuel element's operational lifetime. The European allowance extends intellectual property protection for a core element of Lightbridge's fuel technology across 39 contracting states, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and all major European nuclear markets. The patent covers fuel elements manufactured via additive manufacturing (3D printing), a process that enables the production of complex multi-material zone architectures that are unachievable through conventional fuel fabrication techniques. Combined with Lightbridge's existing U.S. and international patent portfolio, this grant meaningfully expands the Company's IP moat in advanced nuclear fuel. The allowed claims are directed to a fuel element comprising three distinct radial zones of different materials — a first zone extending along the central axis, a second surrounding zone, and a third outermost zone — in which the thickness of both the second and third zones in the radial direction varies along the axial direction. The manufacturing method claims cover the use of additive manufacturing to produce this multi-zone architecture using metallic, ceramic, or cermet fuel systems. The variable zone thickness along the axial direction enables engineers to tailor the radial and axial neutron flux profile within a single element, supporting optimization of reactor performance, safety margin management, and fissile material efficiency throughout the fuel cycle. "Receiving this allowance from the European Patent Office is an important validation of the technical depth and novelty of Lightbridge Fuel™," said Seth Grae, President and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge Corporation. "Europe is home to a significant installed base of nuclear generating capacity, and the countries and utilities advancing nuclear energy as part of their clean energy programs represent a natural market for Lightbridge Fuel. This patent ensures that the fuel element design at the heart of Lightbridge Fuel, with our precise multi-zone architecture and variable radial zone configuration, is protected across those markets as we advance toward commercialization."

Building on their November 2025 agreement, the companies will combine Palantir's advanced AI software with Stagwell's marketing expertise and agentic technology to help enterprises modernize marketing operations, unlock the value of their data and drive business growth. As part of the expansion, Stagwell will serve as a premier marketing transformation partner for Palantir while developing new AI-powered solutions for enterprise customers leveraging Palantir's platforms. "Stagwell and Palantir are bringing together two powerful sets of capabilities to fundamentally transform enterprise marketing," said Mark Penn, Chairman and CEO of Stagwell. "With this partnership, Stagwell is turning its advanced marketing capabilities into compounding advantage for their customers," said Alex Karp, CEO and Co-Founder of Palantir. Palantir's technology will be leveraged within the family of Stagwell's Machine products, including Machine OS, The Knowledge Machine (turns consumer sentiment signals into action), the audience machine (builds audience profiles and creates addressable segments) and The Media Machine (a full-lifecycle agentic media operating system designed to plan, optimize, and measure across platforms). Through Palantir's ontologies and agent framework, the partnership will help power connected workflows, intelligence and activation across the Machines portfolio. Central to the collaboration is a shared commitment to AI sovereignty, ensuring enterprises maintain control over their proprietary data and technology infrastructure. Mural, a startup founded by former Palantir engineers, raises $15 million bid to connect banks to the emerging bot economy

The stablecoin boom has promised to make global commerce faster and cheaper by easing cross-border money transfers. But delivering on that promise remains complicated, as businesses still have to juggle banks, payment providers, and a patchwork of regulations. New York-based startup Mural wants to f...

The stablecoin boom has promised to make global commerce faster and cheaper by easing cross-border money transfers. But delivering on that promise remains complicated, as businesses still have to juggle banks, payment providers, and a patchwork of regulations. New York-based startup Mural wants to fix that problem by offering businesses one place to manage international payments, rather than having to piece together the system themselves. Cofounded by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes in 2022, Mural announced Tuesday that it has raised a $15 million Series A funding round. The startup plans to use the funds to further build out its platform, which allows customers—including payroll providers, software companies and fintechs—to rely on a single account that can hold traditional dollars, local currencies, and stablecoins. "[We are] building this… compliant system of record that allows for businesses and fintechs to launch new financial products on top of us," Toffa, who serves as Mural's CEO, explained. Fintech innovation has reshaped how money moves in recent years, and stablecoins have become part of that shift. These cryptocurrencies, typically designed to track the U.S. dollar, can move across borders in seconds, sometimes only for pennies in network fees. Stablecoin payments reached roughly $400 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up from the same period a year earlier, per a report from global consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal. Their use for international transfers has also grown: cross-border stablecoin flows totaled $220 billion from July 2025 through June 2026, up nearly 78% from the previous 12 months, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis. Tether, the issuer behind the USDT stablecoin, led Mural's Series A, with participation from North Island Ventures. The round brings Mural's total funding to $28 million, following a $5 million seed round in 2022 and additional pre-seed and interim financing from earlier backers. Mural declined to disclose its valuation following its latest fundraising round. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the investment also reflects a bet on AI agents becoming regular handlers of financial services. "Those agents will need access to payment systems that operate around the clock and can reach people across the world," he told Fortune in a written statement. Toffa's interest in international payments began when he visited Togo, his grandfather's home country, when he was 15 years old. His relatives there, who routinely received remittances from his father in the United States, told him that transfers could take weeks to arrive and cost as much as 20% in fees.

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » My view: Don't sell Palantir simply because its stock has soared. But don't hold it blindly, either. Existing shareholders should reassess three things: the company's growth prospects, the return its current valuation can deliver, and the amount of their portfolio tied up in the stock. A great business can remain a great investment for years. But the price you pay, or continue holding at, still matters. Palantir's recent results show why investors are optimistic. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue jumped 93% year over year to $1.94 billion. U.S. commercial revenue surged 149% to $764 million, while U.S. government revenue grew 90% to $809 million. Adjusted operating margin reached 62%, and management raised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 82%. These aren't just impressive growth rates; they instead suggest Palantir is turning demand for artificial intelligence (AI) into substantial revenue while maintaining strong profitability. But strong operating performance doesn't guarantee strong stock returns, which brings us to the more difficult question. Palantir's valuation leaves investors with high expectations to meet. On Oct. 15, 2026, the stock closed at $200.50, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately $482 billion. Its trailing price-to-earnings ratio was around 171. At that valuation, investors aren't merely expecting Palantir to succeed. They're paying a substantial premium for continued success. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores, capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft (MSFT) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon (AMZN) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) got exactly one day in 2016. Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard. Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July. Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring. Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion. Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Little-Known Chip Stock Is the AI Boom's Best-Kept Secret.

No summary available

Everyone knows that GPUs are a strong investment because they make an artificial intelligence (AI) data center run, and most investors are now figuring out that memory matters too. What fewer people think about is the cable. Thousands of accelerators in a single building only work if the data betwee...

Everyone knows that GPUs are a strong investment because they make an artificial intelligence (AI) data center run, and most investors are now figuring out that memory matters too. What fewer people think about is the cable. Thousands of accelerators in a single building only work if the data between them arrives clean, fast, and without a single dropped link, and the company that has become the reference name for that job is not Nvidia or Micron Technology. It is Credo Technology Group (NASDAQ: CRDO), a connectivity chip designer whose stock has more than tripled in three years and still gets a fraction of the attention its customers give it. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Credo's signature product is something called an active electrical cable, or AEC. It looks like a thick copper cable, but it has Credo's chips built into each end to clean up the signal, allowing hyperscalers to connect servers and switches at 800 gigabits per second over copper instead of paying for power-hungry optical transceivers. The company's purple cables are distinctive enough that Credo trademarked the color. It also sells the retimer and digital signal processor chips inside those cables as stand-alone parts, plus optical DSPs, PCIe retimers, and licensed intellectual property. Credo's "little-known" status is mostly a function of what it sells rather than of how much it sells. Revenue in the quarter ended Aug. 1 more than doubled from a year earlier, and the company has gone from licensing firm to hardware supplier for several of the largest cloud operators in about three years. The reason to pay attention right now is that Credo is in the middle of a planned shift from copper to light, and October is when the pieces showed up. In May, it closed its acquisition of DustPhotonics, an Israeli silicon photonics company, which gave Credo an in-house photonic chip capability to go with its existing DSPs and cable systems. Management said at the time that it expects the combined optical portfolio to become a "significant growth driver" in fiscal 2027. Then at the Open Compute Project summit in San Jose this month, Credo unveiled its 1.6-terabit ZeroFlap Active Light Cable. Instead of pushing a few optical channels to extreme speeds, it uses a dense array of tiny light emitters running in parallel at slower rates. The approach is designed to deliver copper-level reliability out to 50 meters, covering a full row of data center racks, while drawing about 30% less power than a comparable copper AEC and weighing a tenth as much.

Collaboration will establish the roadmap for bringing Pony.ai robotaxis to Kazakhstan on the inDrive ride-hailing platform, leveraging the NVIDIA Hyperion and the NVIDIA Halos safety system. ALMATY, Kazakhstan, October 23, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--inDrive, the global mobility and delivery platform, today announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with NVIDIA and Pony.ai, a global leader in the large-scale commercialization of autonomous driving technology, to explore the future of autonomous ride-hailing. Kazakhstan will serve as the first test market. Kazakhstan was chosen first for its regulatory readiness following the creation of the country's first structured legal framework for driverless transport, as part of its "Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence." Combined with Kazakhstan's position as a leading Central Asian economy, this gives the companies a clear basis to assess autonomous ride-hailing in practice. The three companies will evaluate the technical, operational, regulatory and commercial feasibility of offering level 4-ready autonomous vehicles to riders through the inDrive app in Kazakhstan. Pony.ai would provide its seventh-generation (Gen-7) robotaxis, inDrive would provide the ride-hailing platform and run the service, while NVIDIA would support the project with NVIDIA AI infrastructure. The NVIDIA Hyperion is a reference sensor and compute platform for Level 4 autonomous vehicles and robotaxis. The NVIDIA robotaxi platform combines NVIDIA Hyperion with Alpamayo Stack and Halos full-stack safety system to accelerate safe, production-ready autonomy. inDrive and Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in Astana, Kazakhstan's capital, using Pony.ai's Gen-7 robotaxis. Pony.ai's Level 4 autonomous driving technology has been validated through fully driverless commercial operations in major Chinese cities, as well as real-world deployments across Europe, the Middle East and Asia. The Gen-7 robotaxi incorporates multi-sensor fusion, system-level redundancy and fail-operational capabilities to support safe and reliable driverless operations. The launch would follow an agreement with the government of Kazakhstan. Astana, one of Central Asia's fastest-growing capitals, offers a promising environment for autonomous ride-hailing. With a population of approximately 1.7 million and growing demand for urban transportation, the city presents opportunities for robotaxis to complement existing mobility services and offer residents more convenient travel options. Combined with inDrive's established presence in Kazakhstan, the initiative could provide a foundation for exploring autonomous mobility in other markets across the region. Following the initial launch in Astana, the companies will assess whether the approach could be extended to other cities in Kazakhstan as well as other countries where inDrive operates.
